teacher_info.about_teacher: My first experience as a teacher was in my martial arts club in Pittsburgh.  I taught for 10 years.  Though this seems quite different from teaching a language, it was, in fact, excellent preparation for my career as an English teacher.  Learning correct pronunciation involves learning unfamiliar movements.  It is much more a physical skill than an academic exercise.  To achieve fluency in speaking, one cannot carefully think about each word or phrase --- words and phrases must be automatic.  To learn to speak automatically, one must practice regularly and diligently.  I prefer to correct a student's mistakes immediately so that s/he is more likely to remember the correct usage.
teacher_info.teaching_style: In my experience, many students were never taught the basic sounds of English.  For this reason, I always include phonics exercises as part of every class.  When teaching grammar, I focus on the meaning of a particular construction rather than just how to make it.  It is important for students to do exercises that require them to choose between more than one possible grammatical construction.  This replicates real life, where one must choose the construction that will communicate the correct meaning.

There are certain things that make it obvious that you're not a native English speaker. Pronunciation is only one small part of that.

In these sessions, I'll help you fully understand and improve all the areas that will help you speak more naturally like a native speaker.

We will cover:
- pronunciation (of course)
- common phrases, expressions & idioms (including what they mean, correct ways to say them, and appropriate times to use them + when not to use them)
- slang + which slang should not be used in a professional setting (you have to be careful with this)
- proper greetings + how to respond to different greetings
- appropriate greetings to use with your superiors vs. peers or subordinates (You want to be sure to get this right!)
- formal vs. informal language + appropriate times to use each one
- the correct rhythm of the English language + how it's different from your native language
- correct use of emphasis on words in a sentence to convey different meanings
- different ways to introduce yourself (or someone else) depending on if you're in person, on the phone, or via email
- correct use of prepositions, especially in/on/at (These can be confusing for non-native English speakers.)
- correct use of verb tenses (This is one of the biggest ways you can sound more natural right away.)
- how to properly pronounce letters when spelling words (and differences between British & American English)
- other differences between British & American English that you should know, especially depending on who you work with more often
- how to properly say numbers + how it's different depending on the type of number
- how to express units of measurement (like when to use things like carton, container, pack, package, etc.)
- and many more words, phrases, and ways to say things that will help you sound more natural when speaking

Having taught English for 14 years, I can quickly spot the areas you can improve to sound more natural. With my coaching, you will improve quickly.

pro_course_detail.title: English for School Writing
pro_course_detail.description:
I am a native speaker with a midwestern American accent, and I have taught in grade schools, colleges and as an online tutor.

This lesson is for children in 6th through 12th grade who are fluent or almost fluent in English. It will be tailored to meet your child’s unique needs and interests, focusing on improving your child’s understanding of grammar and adding to their vocabulary. I do not intend to teach grammar or vocabulary until I know what they need. I will teach them how to write clearly and vividly as well as how to write strong arguments. In most cases, this will include teaching them logic (argumentation) and outline writing. If your child needs to work on their pronunciation, I can help with that, too.

I teach using my own resources and your child’s corrected work, as well as any writing they do for me. I develop my own Google docs resources to share with students to help them with grammar, vocabulary, etc., and I share those with students and parents via gmail. When your child has written something for a class or taken a grammar or vocabulary test and doesn’t understand what they got wrong, they can share those documents with me so that I can explain and teach them how to avoid mistakes.
  
If your child needs help with  pronunciation, they’ll read articles about topics they’re interested in or resources I’ve shared with them to me. As they make pronunciation mistakes, I’ll correct their pronunciation and give them exercises to complete as homework when needed to improve their pronunciation.

Please let me know if you have any questions about my teaching methods, and please consider having your children take a trial lesson with me to help you all get an idea of whether you think I would be a good fit. 

I look forward to meeting you!

pro_course_detail.title: English Writing for School and Business
pro_course_detail.description:
I’m a native speaker with a midwestern American accent, and I’ve been an English teacher in grade schools, college and an online tutor. 

This lesson is tailored to meet your unique needs and interests, focusing on academic and/or business vocabulary, syntax, grammar and clarity, as well as pronunciation if necessary.  It’s intended for people who are fluent or becoming fluent in English and want to improve their speaking, listening and writing skills for work or school.  I’ll help you perfect up to two written texts per week, and I’ll familiarize you with phrasal verbs, idioms and slang if you’re interested.  I can also help you practice for exams and interviews with common questions and useful techniques. I would also be happy to help you build your online presence in English for sites like LinkedIn.  

Depending on what you're writing, this may also include teaching logic and how logic is related to outline writing. 

I hope you’ll consider taking a trial lesson with me so you can consider whether I will be a good fit for you. I look forward to meeting you!

I've had the opportunity to teach hundreds of students from a variety of countries, ranging from beginners to advanced/fluent. I have taught group lessons and private lessons. Teaching online has shown me that students learn in a variety of ways, some being more effective than others. After each lesson, I provide feedback on what students have done well and the steps they can take to improve their skills. 

One of my other responsibilities is as an academic writing skills tutor for two large universities, where I help students develop their academic English skills and fix grammar, sentence structure, and spelling issues. I do these corrections in British English and American English, depending on the student's preferred writing style. 

Finally, I spend most of my time abroad and am therefore familiar with the difficulties of communicating in a foreign language when you have not developed the necessary skills to communicate clearly and effectively. I am here to help you improve your communication skills so you can avoid the problems and awkward situations I have when doing business, traveling, or any other activity using a foreign language. Best wishes!
